svg.text: FitCheck — Logical Relational Database Schema Diagram (Physical Design)
Normalized Relational Model (3NF) | Foreign Key Constraints, Integrity Rules, Unique Keys, and Weak Entity Mappings
Relational Schema Architectural Legend & Course Mapping Principles:
Autonomous Base Table (Strong Entity with Independent Primary Key e.g., users, brands, garments)
Weak Entity Relational Mapping (Existence-dependent table identified by Owner FK + Discriminator)
Surrogate primary key guaranteeing physical referential efficiency (AUTO_INCREMENT)
Referential integrity link to referenced parent primary key (with CASCADE or RESTRICT rules)
Weak entity partial key (e.g. size_label, measurement_type) forming composite candidate key with Owner FK
Weak Entity Academic Resolution & Relational Correspondence:
• GARMENT_SIZE cannot exist without an owning GARMENT; a size label like "32W 30L" has no standalone meaning.
• Conceptual Key: Composite {garment_id, size_label}. Relational implementation preserves this via UQ(garment_id, size_label).
• Surrogate garment_size_id is retained to prevent bulky compound foreign keys in child tables (purchases, measurements).
• GARMENT_MEASUREMENT is a second-order weak entity dependent on GARMENT_SIZE via UQ(garment_size_id, measurement_type).
• Foreign Key cascades ensure full existence dependency: Deleting a GARMENT deletes all its sizes and all their measurements.
